:_mod-docs-content-type: CONCEPT

[id="model-catalog-source-types_{context}"]
= Model catalog source types

[role='_abstract']
You can configure model catalog sources to control which AI models are available to your organization's data scientists.
{productname-short} supports two types of catalog sources, each with distinct behaviors for model naming, filtering, and management.
Understanding the differences between source types helps you configure include and exclude filters correctly and avoid common misconfiguration errors.

[id="yaml-file-sources_{context}"]
== YAML-file sources

YAML-file sources define models by using a YAML catalog specification stored in a ConfigMap.
The default {org-name} AI and {org-name} AI validated sources are YAML-file sources.

YAML-file sources have the following characteristics:

* Model names use the `__organization__/__model-name__` format, for example, `RedHat/granite-3.1-8b-instruct`.
* Include and exclude filter entries must use the full `__organization__/__model-name__` format.
* You can define multiple organizations in a single YAML-file source.
* YAML-file sources work in both connected and disconnected environments.

[id="hugging-face-sources_{context}"]
== Hugging Face sources

Hugging Face sources sync models from a specified organization on huggingface.co.
Each Hugging Face source connects to a single organization and retrieves the publicly available models from that organization.

Hugging Face sources have the following characteristics:

* Model names use the bare `__model-name__` format, for example, `granite-3.1-8b-instruct`, because the organization is specified separately.
* Include and exclude filter entries use only the model name, without an organization prefix.
* Each Hugging Face source is limited to one organization.
* The allowed organization name is case-sensitive and must match the URL slug from the Hugging Face website, not the display name.
For example, use `meta-llama` from `huggingface.co/meta-llama`, not the display name "Meta Llama".
* Only public, non-gated models are supported for catalog-based deployment.
Private and gated Hugging Face model support is planned for a future release.

[IMPORTANT]
====
Hugging Face sources require network connectivity to huggingface.co to sync models.
In disconnected (air-gapped) environments, Hugging Face sources are not available.
Use YAML-file sources instead.
====

[id="comparison-of-source-types_{context}"]
== Comparison of source types

The following table summarizes the key differences between YAML-file and Hugging Face source types.

.Model catalog source type comparison
[cols="1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Characteristic
|YAML-file source

|Model name format
|`__organization__/__model-name__`
|`__model-name__`

|Include/exclude filter format
|`__organization__/__model-name__`
|`__model-name__`

|Organizations per source

|Private or gated model support
|Not applicable

|===

[id="how-sources-interact-with-catalog-governance_{context}"]
== How sources interact with catalog governance

Model catalog sources feed models into the catalog, and governance controls determine which models are visible to non-administrator users.
The filtering pipeline works as follows:

. Source-level include and exclude filters are applied first, controlling which models from each source are added to the catalog.
. The disallow list is applied next, hiding individually restricted models from non-administrator users regardless of their source.

This means that even if a model passes source-level filters, an administrator can still disallow-list it to enforce organizational policies.
Conversely, a model that is excluded at the source level is never available in the catalog and does not need to be disallow-listed.

[id="dashboard-based-source-management_{context}"]
== Dashboard-based source management

You can manage model catalog sources from the AI Catalog Settings page in the {productname-short} dashboard instead of editing ConfigMaps directly.
The dashboard provides a graphical interface for adding, editing, enabling, disabling, and removing catalog sources of both types.
